## NOTE 14 PROPERTY TRANSACTIONS, NET

Property transaccions, net consisted of the following:

| Year Ended December 31 (In thousands)        |   2004 | 2003       |   2002 |
|----------------------------------------------|--------|------------|--------|
| Gain on sale of North Las Vegas land         |        | $ (36,776) |        |
| Siegfried theatre write-down Mirage The Roy  |        | 1,408      |        |
| Storm damage Beau Rivage                     |        |            |  7,824 |
| Write-off of Detroit development costs       |        |            |  4,754 |
| Impairment of assets to be disposed of.      |    473 | 5,764      |  2,134 |
| Demolition costs                             |  7,057 | 6,614      |        |
| Other net losses on asset sales or disposals |  1,135 | 4,049      |        |
|                                              |  8,665 | $ (18,941) | 14,712 |

In 2004, there were no material unusual property transactions. In 2003 the Company sold 315 acres of land in North Las Nevada near Shadow Creek for approximately $55 million, which resulted in pretax gain of approximately 537 million. Also in 2003, the Company recorded write-downs and impairments of assets abandoned or replaced with new construction, primarily at MGM Grand Las in preparation for new restaurants and the new theatre. Prior to 2003, the Company classified and losses on routine asset sales or disposals as a non-operating item at some resorts and as an operating item at other resorts\_ Management believes the preferable presentation of these items is as an element of operating income. Prior statements have not been reclassified as such transactions were not material in the periods. Until 2003, demolition costs were typically capitalized as part of new construction. The Company began expensing demolition costs on major construction projects as incurred on January 1, 2003, and is accounting for this in policy prospectively. Demolition costs were not material in periods. Demolition costs in 2004 and 2003 relate primarily to preparacion for the Bellagio standard room remodel, Bellagio expansion and new theatre at MGM Grand Las Vegas. Vegas, Vegas gains period prior change prior In 2002, Tropical Storm Isidore caused property damage at Beau totaling $8 million; including clean-up costs. The amount of the write-down for damaged assets was determined based on the net book value of the assets and engineering estimates. In connection with the revised development agreement in Detroit, the Company wrote off $5 million; which was the net book value of previously incurred development costs associated with the riverfront permanent casino site (S9 million), offset by previously accrued obligations no longer under the revised development impairments of assets abandoned or replaced with new construction. Rivage required

## NOTE 15 RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS

The Companys related party transactions consisted of the following revenues (expenses):

| Ended December 31 (In thousands) Year                             | 2004      | 2003    | 2002    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|---------|---------|
| Hotel and other revenue from related parties                      | 416       | 871     | 764     |
| License fees to entities under common ownership                   | (1,000)   | (1,000) | (1,000) |
| Professional fees to directors or firms affiliated with directors | (4,084)   | (1,551) | (1,815) |
| Other related party expenses                                      | (62)      | (468)   | (224)   |
|                                                                   | $ (4,730) | (2,148) | (2,275) |

At December 31, 2004, the Company owed $2 million for legal fees to firm affiliated with one of the Companys directors. The Company also engaged in transactions with its unconsolidated affiliates. In each of 2004 and 2003, the Company Monte Carlo $4 million as a result of closing the tram between Bellagio and Monte Carlo in preparation for the Bellagio expansion The Company leases two acres of land to Borgata and received $1 million in each of 2004, 2003 and 2002 under this lease. Borgata is required to pay for a portion of the master plan improvements at Renaissance Pointe; and the Company is responsible for environmental cleanup costs incurred by Borgata. The net amount reimbursed to the Company under these arrangements for the years ended December 31, 2004, 2003 and 2002 was $1 million; $10 million and $8 million, respectively: paid
